provenance.source: Sheet1 (worksheet 'GSTR-3B') VBA: Validate_json, export_in_json_format, isValidAmount, isAfterPartCGoLive, isAfterEcoSupGoLive, removeInterSupValidation; layouts and lists read from the workbook itself.
provenance.v56_to_v58_diff: One line: removeInterSupValidation() moved its first arm from (yr>=2025 && mnthIndex>=1) to (yr>=2025 && mnthIndex>=8) — the 3.2 auto-population (and inter_sup drop) deferred from April 2025 to November 2025.

table_311.note: 3.1.1 rows unhide and eco_dtls is emitted from July 2022 (CR-21773C: yr==2022 && mnthIndex>=4 || yr>=2023).

inter_sup_dropped.note: CR28570A/V5.8: 3.2 is auto-populated from GSTR-1/1A/IFF, manual entry locked, the inter_sup block omitted from the JSON and its IGST rule skipped. Literal: (yr>=2025 && mnthIndex>=8) || (yr>=2026 && any month) — contiguous from November 2025.

outward.applies_to: every input cell of tables 3.1, 3.1.1 and the whole 3.2 amount region
outward.divergence: DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE. The utility's isAfterPartCGoLive() is literally (yr == 2024 && mnthIndex >= 6) — no yr >= 2025 arm — so V5.8 REJECTS negatives in these tables for FY 2025-26 onward while its own cell validations and the portal accept them. The window here is open-ended from September 2024, which is what the gate obviously meant. (A second bug makes the utility's whitelist moot when the gate IS live: 'IsInArray(a,rng) Or IsInArray(a,rng2) Or IsInArray(a,rng3) >= 0' parses as ...Or (x >= 0), and IsInArray returns -1 = truthy when absent, so every cell passes as negative-allowed.)

itc.note: The working ElseIf whitelist, verbatim: table 4(A) rows 31-35 (all four columns, including the structurally blocked D31/E31/D32/E32) plus 4(D)(2) row 42. Rows 37-38 (ITC reversed) and row 41 (4(D)(1)) are NOT negative-allowed. The gate is (yr==2022 && mnthIndex>=10) || yr>=2023 — mnthIndex is FISCAL (April=1), so index 10 is JANUARY: negatives from January 2023, not October 2022.

negatives.never: tables 5 (D48:E49), 5.1 interest (C65:F65), late fee (D66:E66), itc_rev (C37:F38), itc_inelg row 41 (C41:F41)

sup_details.note: Table 3.1 rows 11-15. Emission writes all five keys per row; cells absent below are structurally blocked (merged/locked) and emit 0. F11 and F14 are sheet formulas =E11/=E14 (SGST mirrors CGST).

itc_elg.note: Emission writes iamt/camt/samt/csamt for EVERY ty row, blocked or blank cells emitting 0 — IMPG/IMPS carry camt:0, samt:0. E33/E34/E35/E37/E41/E42 are =D formulas; E38 is the one real SGST input in table 4.

itc_net.formula: per column: SUM(ROUND(each itc_avl cell, 2)) - SUM(ROUND(each itc_rev cell, 2))
itc_net.note: The VBA exports the CACHED C39:F39 formula results, rounded again. This implementation computes the formula (identical whenever the sheet formulas are intact) and warns when a cached value drifts from it.

inward_sup.note: Blank cells are force-written to 0 before emission, so both rows always appear with both keys.

ltfee_details.note: The late-fee row is HIDDEN in the sheet yet exported; the only keys emitted UNROUNDED and omitted when blank (both blank -> an empty object).

pos_region.pos_payload_form: the two-digit prefix of the dropdown text, emitted as a STRING
pos_region.inclusion: a row enters a sub-array iff its POS is non-empty AND at least one of that pair's two cells is non-empty; the blank member is coerced to 0 (the VBA writes the 0 back into the sheet). Empty sub-arrays are still emitted.

rules.checks: length exactly 15; first two characters numeric, < 39 and != 28; regex [0-9]{2}[a-zA-Z]{5}[0-9]{4}[a-zA-Z][1-9A-Za-z][Zz1-9A-Ja-j][0-9a-zA-Z] (unanchored in the VBA, but the length check makes it equivalent to anchored). NO check-digit verification.

rules.note: OURS, not the utility's: the mod-36 check digit the rest of this project validates. A GSTIN passing the utility's rules but failing the checksum is almost certainly a typo the portal will reject.

rules.checks: blank is valid (exports 0); otherwise numeric and within [min, 9999999999999.99], min per the negatives windows. The utility's error text promises a two-decimal-places check that its code never performs; decimals beyond 2 are accepted and rounded at export.
rules.message: Please enter a valid amount. Field accepts only numeric value. Maximum: 13 digits with two decimal places.
Please enter Taxable value or amount of integrated tax in Table 3.2 for the selected Place of Supply
Please select Place of Supply in Table 3.2 for which Taxable value or amount of integrated tax is entered

rules.note: The utility blocks duplicates live (Worksheet_Change + Application.Undo); on a finished workbook this reports instead.
rules.message: Duplicate entries not allowed for Place of Supply(State/UT)

rules.note: OURS: the utility's dropdown makes an unknown POS untypeable; a hand-built workbook can carry one.

rules.checks: SUM(D88:D124) + SUM(F88:F124) + SUM(H88:H124) <= D11 + D22. From 072022 the rule also requires the 3.2 total to be non-zero before firing (igstTotal <> 0); before 072022 the comparison is against D11 alone with no zero guard. Only IGST is checked — taxable value never is.
rules.message: Total amount of Integrated Tax in section 3.2 should be less than or equal to the sum of Integrated tax declared in section 3.1(a) and 3.1.1(i)

rules.note: OURS: the utility enforces SGST == CGST purely by sheet formulas (F11, F14, F22, E33, E34, E35, E37, E41, E42). A workbook with broken formulas exports the mismatch verbatim — this warns instead of silently shipping it. E38 is excluded: it is a genuine input.
OURS: cached C39:F39 disagreeing with the recomputed itc_net formula — a broken-formula signal.

emission.ret_period: MMYYYY; January/February/March take the financial year's END year, all other months its start year
emission.defaults: every fixed-block key is always emitted, blank cells as 0; only ltfee_details keys and the inter_sup block are ever omitted
emission.rounding: Application.WorksheetFunction.Round(x, 2) — half away from zero on the cell's double value — on every amount except the two late-fee cells
emission.clean_json_divergence: DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE: this implementation emits compact clean JSON (payload writer) in the same key order. The utility's file carries CRLF line endings, stray blank lines, a bare CR inside empty braces/brackets left by its trailing-comma chop, and a space before the gstin colon only — all legal-JSON whitespace noise. Captured files are compared semantically (parse both sides), not byte-for-byte.

filename.note: The month is the dropdown text verbatim; the year is the FY START year even for January-March, so the name and ret_period disagree by one year in those months. The utility writes under %USERPROFILE%\Desktop\GSTR\GSTR3B_JSON\{month}\; this implementation writes into --output.

notes.text: Legal name (C6) is entered on the form but never validated and never exported.
The utility has no import path at all — it is write-only, and errors from the portal stay on the portal.

The FY dropdown ends at 2026-27: the workbook expires. Table 5's inter-state Total (D50) is a hardcoded literal 0. Hidden rows 74-82 ship with leftover test data. The POS list omits code 28 and misspells 31-Lakshdweep and 36-Telengana.
A GSTIN with state code 97 (Other Territory) can never validate (prefix must be < 39), although 97 is a selectable POS in 3.2.
gstr3b.gstin_checksum, gstr3b.pos_unknown, gstr3b.sgst_mirrors_cgst and gstr3b.itc_net_drift are additional warnings this implementation raises; the utility has no equivalent.
